author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Defending Premier League champion Arsenal maintained a perfect start Saturday with a 2-0 victory at Sunderland, moving to 12 points from four matches. Goalkeeper David Raya changed the match by saving Enzo Le Fee’s penalty in the 55th minute, and Arsenal took the lead two minutes later.

Bruno Guimaraes scored his first Arsenal goal with a curling finish after coming on as a substitute. Bukayo Saka added a penalty deep into stoppage time after Reinildo Mandava received a second yellow card for the foul. Sunderland challenged the leaders for long stretches but could not convert its clearest opportunity.

The result separated Arsenal from several expected title rivals. Liverpool drew 0-0 with Fulham, its third draw in four league matches, while Chelsea needed a second-half equalizer to draw Hull City 2-2. Nottingham Forest won 2-1 at Aston Villa, and Ipswich edged 10-man Crystal Palace 3-2 in the day’s other notable results.
dek: David Raya saved a penalty before Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka scored to give the defending champions 12 points from four matches.
headline: Arsenal stays perfect with 2-0 win at Sunderland
